title: Challenge/content and result workflows still need rehearsal evidence for fixture parity and release completeness

original_titles.title: Rules PDF not generated at publish time (PUB-02b S2)

problem: The Option B fixture is described as mirroring Option A, but the repo audit flags that equivalence is not independently certified and CTF quest/token variety is below the target. Rules PDF/content publishing artifacts are also not fully automated. These are content/operations acceptance items rather than core backend defects.
impact: Unequal challenge difficulty or incomplete flags can produce unfair outcomes. A rules document or answer pack that is not versioned at publish time can diverge from what participants accepted.

evidence_paths: backend/seed.py: challenge fixture and GT seeds
verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Run independent challenge review on both repository variants using a fixed rubric: defect count, severity, location density, root-cause diversity, test coverage, runtime behavior and solve-time estimate.
Reconcile every planted flag/bug and hidden test to the authoritative GT manifest; make any token-in-history or additional flag quest explicit in the published scoring design.
Generate a versioned rules PDF and challenge manifest from the same source/config used by the API; store content hash and acceptance version.
Conduct a blind pilot with teams who did not author the challenge and record observed difficulty/score distribution. Adjust only through a versioned owner-approved revision.
Block READY until final content packages, reviewer approvals, score policy and rules artifacts are frozen.

acceptance_criteria: Two independent reviewers certify A/B equivalence.
All flags/bugs/tests map to an authoritative GT record.
Published rules/content hash matches the accepted and deployed version.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
